description: A byte-aligned binary is not necessarily UTF-8. Elixir rejects JSON.encode!(<<255>>) with {:invalid_byte, 255}; fz currently succeeds and emits <<34, 255, 34>>, which is not a valid JSON string. lib/json.fz documents that encode!/1 accepts a binary and only rejects non-byte-aligned bitstrings, so the public contract also misses this boundary. Decide the failure reason, validate binary string values at the one encode!/1 binary entry shared by binary object keys, prove values and keys against Elixir on interp/run/build, and update the encoding docs. Keep this separate from fz-5xp.99: that ticket escapes C0 bytes inside valid UTF-8 and explicitly leaves ordinary bytes unchanged.

comments.text: Implemented as 7446a4fb9. Json.encode!/1 now sends every binary value through Utf8.from_bytes/1 and encodes only the branded success value; binary object keys retain the same path through encode!/1. Invalid byte-aligned binaries and partial bitstrings now halt uniformly with {:json_encode, :invalid_utf8, value}. Added Elixir-asserted abort fixtures for invalid values and keys across interp/JIT/AOT, updated the prior non-byte-aligned pin, the Json contract, and negative-oracle documentation. Proven red before implementation on all six value/key doors. Final green: cargo test --test fixture_matrix (694), cargo test --workspace --lib (2018 + 257 passed; 6 ignored), cargo test --workspace --doc, cargo test --test fz2_cli (30), cargo test --test aot_variadic_open (1), cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo fmt --check, git diff --check, and pre-commit gates. Dogfooding exposed the symmetric decoder bug; after a board search it was reproduced against Elixir and filed as fz-5xp.102.

title: Json.encode! emits invalid JSON for a byte-aligned non-UTF-8 binary
